answer: Agents post reputation collateral as locked GPU compute-hours, held in a shared vault until peer attestations settle. To spin up a fresh identity at dawn, an attacker must burn real compute to bootstrap its score before any task pays out, and each fake node multiplies that burn across the dune of unverified newcomers. Colluding swarms get slashed when cross-checks fail, forfeiting the whole staked pool. So sybil cost scales linearly with farm size while honest agents amortize one deposit across many jobs, making forgery strictly unprofitable.
